notes.240v.16: 240v.21: skipilse, rendered 'part', is uncertain. 240v.31: 'sæn fræmir meer', rendered 'beyond that, greater still', is uncertain.
notes.245v.15: 245v.32: kranka mæn, literally 'sick' or 'weak men'; the answer shows that the damned are meant. 245v.46: 'aff en gudhlik ræt', rendered 'out of godly righteousness', is uncertain. *kranka*, literally 'weak' or 'sick', is taken as 'wicked', against the righteous in the answer.

this reason, that all the damned should receive there
their wages. The disciple asked: When did he make the angels? The master
answered: At the time when he said: Now let there be light.
They are called light for this reason, that they have no
part in human nature, but their nature
is spiritual. The disciple asked: Do angels have names?
The master answered: There is so much wisdom in them
by God's grace that they have no need of names.
Michael and Gabriel are not names but by-names
given them by men. The disciple asked:
In what was Lucifer against God? The master answered:
In this, that in the same moment that he was created
he understood himself to be worthier than
any angel; therefore he wished not only
to be God's equal but, beyond that, greater still.
Therefore in the same moment that he was created
he fell from heaven and to the bottom of hell.
And just as he was before the fairest of all angels,
so he also became the most loathsome of all devils.
The disciple asked: Was he long in heaven? The master
answered: Not one full hour. The disciple asked: Why not
longer? The master answered: Because he could not
be [there] longer. The disciple asked: Why did the
others fall with him? The master answered: Because
they obeyed him more than God. The disciple asked:
Why do they not come out of there? The master answered: Because
just as no one caused them to come there,
so no one can bring it about that they come out of there.

The master answered: Because their soul is new and they are
eager, while old people are weighed down with sorrow and cannot
learn so well. The disciple asked: Does a person have an angel as
keeper? The master answered: When the soul and the body come together,
then it gets an angel as keeper. The disciple asked:
Does the devil bear envy toward man? The master answered: Yes; wherever
sin is done, there the devil is egging on; and whatever
person is overcome by the devil comes
to hell and never [out] from there. The disciple asked: Is it to the soul
in any way harmful that the body is buried in heathen ground? The master
answered: In whatever way a righteous person dies, or however
they are buried, they are pleasing to God. The disciple asked: Is
it of any help to them that they are buried in consecrated ground?
The master answered: The ground becomes holy from holy men
being buried in it. But for those who are in torment
it avails them greatly that they are buried in the churchyard, because of
the masses and other good works that are done in the
holy church. The disciple asked: Does it harm wicked men? The master
answered: Yes, greatly. All those who come to hell, for them
the prayer of righteous men avails nothing. One reads that devils
often throw damned bodies out of churchyards.
The disciple asked and said: Jesus Christ reward you for that, master.
Now I ask you, master, to tell me how
righteous souls part from the body. The master answered: Just
as a bridegroom comes to fetch his bride with
great honour, so too comes the angel who
guarded the soul, to fetch her to paradise. The disciple asked: Do
all souls come there? The master answered: Those who are chosen.
The disciple asked: Which are they? The master answered: They are
those who do more than is commanded them, such as
martyrs and monks and virgins; it is not commanded them,
but they do it out of godly righteousness and keep it well;
they have their heaven ready. But other good
souls come to another high joy until Judgement Day,
and after Judgement Day both the righteous and the chosen come
to heaven. And if there is anyone who has not fully
atoned for his sins, he is delivered into his angel's hand,
and the angel delivers him to the devil to torment him;
yet he torments the soul no more and no longer than the angel
wills. The disciple asked: What is the fire of purgatory? The master
